issues.body: The round-2 defect remains in read_varint. At i == 9, payload.checked_shl(63) returns Some whenever the shift count is valid, even when payload > 1; Rust's shift discards the significant high bits. Consequently, a terminal tenth byte such as 0x02 can be accepted and normalized to a smaller u64, contradicting the documented rejection of over-64-bit values and the fail-closed lookup_multihash contract. No added test exercises this boundary.
issues.fix_hint: Before combining the tenth byte, reject i == 9 when payload > 1, or use checked arithmetic that detects value overflow rather than only an invalid shift count. Add tests for the maximal valid u64 varint and invalid terminal tenth-byte payloads such as 0x02 and 0x7f, including a parse_multihash or lookup_multihash assertion proving the public path rejects them.
issues.title: Ten-byte varints still overflow u64 and decode as another value

verdict.summary: Round 3 is stagnant: the same major fail-closed varint overflow remains. On the tenth byte, checked_shl(63) validates only the shift amount and silently discards payload bits above bit 63, so terminal payloads greater than 1 can be accepted as a different u64 value. The tests still omit the maximal-valid and overflowing tenth-byte boundaries.
